subject: the Number of Markers for QTL

messages.author: e2fc16912ef048ff
messages.subject: the Number of Markers for QTL
parts:
Hi,

I am confused about the number of markers to analysis. I have 180 individuals with around 600,000 SNPs and have constructed a genetic map based on them. These SNPs were retained by a set of data cleaning processed. The genetic map consists of 5000 unique loci with all these SNPs where some SNPs located in the same place in a linkage group. 

Now  I'm not sure whether it is necessary to conduct QTL mapping with such a large number of markers. Is this just a time-consuming program if all markers are kept? If there is no need to analyse this with so much data, how should I filter markers?

Thanks,

Syue

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] the Number of Markers for QTL
parts:
It depends on the type of cross and the size of the genome. In recombinant inbred lines or an advanced intercross population, it could be good to have very dense markers. But in a backcross or intercross, there's not much value in having markers that are <1 cM apart.

I would start with findDupMarkers() and cut down on markers that have identical data.
There's also pickMarkerSubset() which picks out a set of markers with no two markers closer than some chosen distance.

karl
